lxc_4a1b4269bb0cf982.text: Most coffee drinks in an Australian café start with espresso.

lxc_32b92e4e47c2deed.text: You will learn what espresso is, how cafés build drinks from it, and why every new barista must learn the café's own recipe.

lxc_075df86b56b14d7a.text: Espresso is not one special bean.

lxc_e06500f7a6a4f908.text: It is a way to make coffee.

lxc_c03780a8968d50e8.text: A machine pushes hot water through finely ground coffee under pressure.

lxc_f166894e499285cd.text: The result is a small, strong drink called an espresso shot.

lxc_f967dbe105334a3c.text: A café can use different beans and roast levels for espresso.

lxc_0848cef8351826fc.text: The word espresso tells us about the brewing method, not the country, bean, or roast.

lxc_f1022f35852d0e7e.text: A dark-roasted bean is not automatically espresso, and a lighter-roasted bean can also be used in an espresso machine.

lxc_e10c1d83204999f1.text: The espresso shot is the base of many Australian café drinks.

lxc_84df5874a4b3b98c.text: A short black is espresso by itself.

lxc_e0e100d7ec765b49.text: A long black adds hot water.

lxc_865f681d3a931c2b.text: A flat white, latte, and cappuccino add textured milk in different amounts and styles.

lxc_2e84979873bb8bce.text: A mocha adds chocolate and milk.

lxc_e4f3be93f6b09535.text: Some cafés also serve espresso over ice or use it in cold milk drinks.

lxc_99af9318661e9869.text: The order may sound complicated, but the barista can listen for the drink base and the added parts.

lxc_6d14141d27bff534.text: For example, a mocha needs espresso, chocolate, and milk.

lxc_b3062d6ae730b7a5.text: A long black needs espresso and water.

lxc_b8f407a16de13250.text: Making espresso is only one part of a barista's work.

lxc_4c0d5b097b70130c.text: A barista grinds coffee, checks the grinder, prepares the coffee in the basket, starts the shot, and tastes the result.

lxc_ae6ac1e6c663acc3.text: The barista also textures milk, cleans the machine, keeps the work area safe, and manages customer orders.

lxc_315876b8dcb6b8d8.text: Heat, humidity, and the age of the beans can change how quickly a shot runs.

lxc_0559d505c945bada.text: For this reason, a barista watches the coffee and adjusts the grinder when needed.

lxc_ee90a28f30ab50ae.text: Good training teaches the worker how to notice a problem and make one careful change.

lxc_bdc032a3d295f88f.text: Every café has a house recipe.

lxc_54d469f149b6deeb.text: The recipe tells the barista how much ground coffee to use, how much espresso to make, and how long the shot should take.

lxc_53ce85b56ce527e2.text: It may also tell the worker how many shots go into each cup size.

lxc_b449c51e93449536.text: One café may use 18 grams of ground coffee.

lxc_403932ad5b2edf9f.text: A large flat white may have two shots in one café and a different recipe in another.

lxc_4d1e386f84bc0a3e.text: A new worker should not guess.

lxc_4e4a3bf7a8385615.text: The professional action is to ask, watch, measure, and follow the café's system.

lxc_90af07211adf89ca.text:
- How much ground coffee do you use here?
- How many shots go into this cup size?
- Could you show me one before I try?

lxc_d3a7fd23b19aefe3.text: She asks the head barista about the espresso recipe before making a flat white.
